key_concepts: Earth is composed of crust, mantle, outer core, and inner core.
The crust is Earth's thin, solid outermost layer made of silicate minerals.
The mantle is a thick layer made of silicate minerals.
The outer core is liquid and made of an iron-nickel alloy.
The inner core is solid and made of an iron-nickel alloy.
Temperature and pressure increase toward Earth's center.
The mantle is the thickest layer and the crust is the thinnest.
Volcanoes are vents where molten rock from Earth's interior erupts onto the surface.
Great heat and pressure develop underground due to the weight of overlying layers.
Magma pushes through weak spots in Earth's outer layer and bursts out.
Volcanic eruptions release energy, pressure, and gases from Earth's interior.
Volcanoes can have severe impacts on communities, but following alerts can reduce risk.
